newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president prepares TV address on funds.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president prepares TV address on funds.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam's scheduled address to the nation on Friday on his 1992 campaign spending will be broadcast live on television, a Blue House official said.
"President Kim Young-sam will give a live television speech at 10.00 a.m. (0100 GMT)," said the official, who declined to be identified. He gave no details of the speech.

Opposition parties allege that Kim's campaign was partly bankrolled by the scandal-ridden Hanbo Group and his predecessor Roh Tae-woo, who is now in jail for bribery and other crimes. They say campaign spending far exceeded legal limits.
Kim agreed on Tuesday to make a national address after the opposition called for an independent day inquiry by parliament, and demanded the president apologise.

Only last week, Kim had appeared to rule out any public statement. An aide quoted him as saying that records of election spending no longer existed, and digging up the issue would only do more harm to the nation.

Political analysts do not believe Friday's address will go into financial details, which could leave the president open to legal action after he steps down at the end of his single term next February.
Instead, the analysts say Kim is likely to express regret for old-style money politics and call for reform. At the same time he would aplogise over the Hanbo scandal.
The collapse of Hanbo's steelmaking unit in January uncovered a web of corruption involving Kim's son, who was arrested this month, and his top aides.
